op_pv_disposition.rationale: PV-0's lightweight scope (file/inventory existence) is appropriate because Phase 0 tasks have no PRD AC bindings (per Plan T0.1/T0.2/T0.3 'Satisfies AC: N/A'). The plan-template's 'validator per phase' rule is structurally satisfied by PV-0's three C-criteria mapped to T0.1/T0.2/T0.3 L1/L2/L3 evidence. Folding Phase 0 into Phase 1 would conflate setup-baseline checks with feature-delivery checks and is rejected. No action required; PV-0 stands as authored.

Manual-review checkpoint logging convention for PV-6.C7 and PV-8.C5 reviewer-judgment events is appropriately operational-time discretion. Both checkpoints already cite ADR-0065 D-8 substance-heuristic posture and kill-criteria (>30% inter-reviewer disagreement across N≥3 runs triggers structural-mandate extension). The validator-output ledger schema for reviewer_judgment events does not need Plan-time codification; per the kill-criteria tracking surface, the calibration corpus accumulates as runs execute. Routes to operational discretion; first ~3 manual-review events build the corpus per ADR-0065. Optional future feature run can formalize the schema if drift emerges.

Controlled-execution-lane definition for AT-027's NFR-1 5000 ms performance test is operational-discretion. The Plan's OP-Plan-2 disposition commits to inline timing in review-architecture-auditor's own logging (per PV-4.C6 'inline timing in auditor's own logging'). AT-027's determinism notes acknowledge flake risk and mitigate via median-of-3 with controlled execution lane. The 'controlled execution lane' literal does not require codification; PV-4.C6's 'warning on first failure (jitter possible); blocking if median across 3 separate runs >5000 ms' provides the explicit escalation rubric. Routes to operational discretion; AT-027 inline timing harness is the documented proxy until controlled-execution-lane convention is needed.
